title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the previous page). A is a Dedekind ring with fraction field K. A 'Dieudonné category' C over A is an A-linear category equivalent to P(O), the category of rank-1 projective modules over an order O. Here O = End(X) for a chosen object X, and O is a maximal order in a central simple K-algebra. The previous page established three facts:
- Equivalence classes of strictly Dieudonné categories correspond to Br(K).
- The A-linear equivalences C → C' form a 'catégorie torseur' under the A-linear autoequivalences of C.
- Once C ≅ P(O) and C' ≅ P(O'), the equivalences correspond to O'–O bimodules that are invertible (projective of rank 1) on each side. Composition of equivalences corresponds to tensor product of bimodules.

This page does three things.

(1) It packages the autoequivalences End(C) into a Gr-catégorie, i.e. a categorical group or 2-group. Fixing X turns this into the monoidal groupoid of 'bi-invertible' A-central O-bimodules under ⊗_O. Grothendieck first wrote 'groupoïde de Brandt', then crossed it out.

(2) He lists the Sinh-type invariants of this 2-group:
- the group of isomorphism classes, Brd(O), which he calls the 'groupe de Brandt'. In modern terms this is the central Picard group Pic_A(O) of invertible bimodules (Fröhlich's Picent / Pic of an order).
- the group Aut(id_C), which equals the units of the centre of O. Here that is A^*.
- the action of the first group on the second, given by σ(λ)x = xλ for x ∈ L. It is trivial because λ is central and the bimodules are A-central ('moralement σ(λ) = xλx^{-1} = λ').
- the canonical class ξ ∈ H^3(Brd(O), O^{♮*}), the k-invariant or associativity class.

This is exactly the classification of Gr-categories by (π0, π1, action, H^3 class) later written up in Hoàng Xuân Sính's thesis (1975).

(3) Dieudonné categories that are equivalent to one another form a 2-groupoid D. Its automorphism Gr-categories ('Gr-catégories fondamentales') are these Brandt 2-groups. D is 2-equivalent to a 2-groupoid Brd built as follows:
- objects: the orders O in a given class;
- 1-morphisms: bi-invertible bimodules ('bitorseurs bi-inversibles');
- 2-morphisms: isomorphisms of bimodules;
- composition: ⊗.

In other words, this is a categorification of Brandt's groupoid of normal ideals between maximal orders, i.e. the Morita 2-groupoid. The next page notes that the 2-functor Brd → D, O ↦ P(O), is a 2-equivalence without a natural quasi-inverse. It then passes to gerbes of banalisations with lien G_m, recovering the Brauer class à la Giraud.

The purpose is a Tannakian-style or 'motivic' description of the Brauer group and its 2-categorical automorphism data, in the arithmetic Galois theory of motives.
errors: Indexing of homotopy invariants is reversed relative to the standard convention. For the groupoid End(C), the isomorphism classes form π0 and Aut(id) is π1. Grothendieck writes Brd(O) = π1 and O^{♮*} = π0. This is consistent only if End(C) is viewed as a one-object 2-groupoid, shifting the indices by one, and he does not say so.
He writes O^{♮*} = End(id_C). In fact End(id_C) is the whole centre O^♮ (a monoid). Its units, Aut(id_C), equal O^{♮*}.
The class ξ is asserted but not computed. Nothing is said about whether it vanishes for maximal orders.

ideas.what: Autoequivalences of a linear category of projective modules form a categorical group, identified with invertible bimodules under tensor product
ideas.modern_name: Picard 2-group / Picard groupoid of a (noncommutative) ring; Morita theory
ideas.usually_credited_to: Morita, Bass (Pic of noncommutative rings, 1960s); Fröhlich (1973) for orders
ideas.where_published: Sinh's thesis (1975, under Grothendieck) treats Gr-categories in general; not known to me in Grothendieck's own published texts

ideas.what: Classification of a Gr-category by π0, π1, the action and a class in H^3(π0, π1)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Hoàng Xuân Sính (thesis 1975, problem posed by Grothendieck); cf. Eilenberg–MacLane / Teichmüller H^3 obstructions
ideas.where_published: Attributed to Grothendieck via Sinh's thesis; Grothendieck mentions Gr-categories in Pursuing Stacks (unsure of precise passage)

ideas.what: Groupe de Brandt = group of classes of bi-invertible bimodules over a maximal order; Brandt groupoid of orders categorified to a 2-groupoid with bimodules as 1-cells
ideas.modern_name: Central Picard group Pic_A(O) / Picent; Morita bicategory of orders
ideas.usually_credited_to: Brandt (1927) for the groupoid of ideals; Fröhlich (1973) for Picent of orders

ideas.what: 2-groupoid D of Dieudonné categories is 2-equivalent to the 2-groupoid of orders, bimodules and isomorphisms, but with no natural inverse 2-functor
ideas.modern_name: Morita 2-equivalence (bicategory of rings, bimodules, intertwiners restricted to invertibles)

missed.claim: The canonical k-invariant ξ ∈ H^3(Pic_A(O), A^*) of the Picard 2-group of a maximal order over a Dedekind ring is introduced but never computed. For an Azumaya O, Pic_A(O) reduces to Pic(A), and the resulting strictly commutative Picard category splits, so ξ = 0. For ramified maximal orders the extra ramification classes could in principle carry a nontrivial associator; an explicit treatment of this is not known to me.
missed.quote: A [?] une classe canonique ξ∈H^3(Brd(O), O^{G*})
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a modest arithmetic question about 2-groups attached to orders. It matters for fusion-category and Brauer–Picard-type computations, but it is likely easy and possibly folklore.

missed.claim: A historical point: the notion 'Gr-catégorie' and its H^3 classification appear here in notes catalogued as 1965 (date uncertain, perhaps up to c.1977). If the 1965 date holds, this predates Sinh's thesis and shows the idea arising from the arithmetic of Brandt groupoids and Brauer groups in the motivic Galois project.
missed.quote: On obtient ainsi, en termes de C, une Gr-catégorie ... Il lui correspond les invariants
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It documents the origin of 2-group classification in Grothendieck's motivic and Brauer-group work, which is relevant for the history of higher category theory.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics is Morita/Picard-2-group material and is routine today. The Gr-category classification is already credited to Grothendieck via Sinh. The interest is mainly historical: an early, arithmetically motivated appearance of the 2-group with its H^3 invariant, and the categorified Brandt groupoid.
transcription_corrections: 'catégories C de Deligne' should read 'catégories C de Dieudonné', consistent with the previous page's 'catégories de Dieudonné'.
'O^{G*}' should be 'O^{♮*}' (units of the centre), as on the previous page.
'2-groupoïde D' with D written above; 'Gr-catégories fondamentales' rather than a list of invariants.
The crossed-out phrase in the first line probably reads 'Gr, pic', i.e. Grothendieck hesitated between 'Gr-catégorie' and 'catégorie de Picard'.
